Serving as the host city for the Olympic Games is a highly contested honor with the multitude of benefits. [[1]] Moreover, visitors attending the events boost local and domestic businesses. It is also a hard-earned opportunity for the host city and country to showcase their technological advancements and cultural heritage to the world.
To be crowned the host city for the Olympics involves passing a rigorous selection process governed by the International Olympic Committee. [[2]] The committee then assesses those proposals based on various criteria such as existing infrastructure, financial capabilities, and commitment to Olympic values. Shortlisted cities undergo further inspection and deliberation before the final decision is made.
However, with such an irresistible glory also come downsides and controversies from time to time. [[3]] That is, some cities are believed to have bribed officials to win their favor. Besides, construction projects specifically meant for the Olympic events can cause environmental degradation, displacement of communities, and labor exploitation. [[4]] Managing the stadiums hence places a tremendous burden on the government budget. All things considered, it is reasonable to conclude that despite the allure of hosting, the decision remains a difficult issue with complex trade-offs.

options_bank.A: In fact, the bidding process itself is not immune to accusations of corruption and lack of transparency.
options_bank.B: Ironically, many of these venues fall into decay after the games due to a lack of use.
options_bank.C: Cities put in detailed bids outlining their plans for venue construction, transportation, security, and sustainability initiatives.
options_bank.D: The mission requires extensive infrastructure upgrade, which guarantees job creation as well as increased investment.
